Say: O chosen ones of God, be steadfast in the Cause of your Lord, the All-Merciful, in such wise that the winds of trials shall not move you, and be ye of those who are firmly rooted in God's Cause. Gather ye in the assemblies of fellowship and remember this Prisoner Who hath been afflicted amidst the hypocrites. Gather ye around that Name. Beware lest ye be scattered, for the wolves lurk behind you with great cunning. Trust ye in God in all matters and shun the wayward. Should ye find one through whose heart the breezes of the All-Merciful have wafted, associate with him and remind him of this mighty Remembrance.

Beware lest ye sorrow over anything or be troubled in adversity and tribulation. By God! We have ordained for you in Our most exalted Kingdom a station of glorious and lofty rank. Be ye united amongst yourselves, for through unity shall the Cause of your Lord, the Mighty, the All-Bestowing, be made manifest, if ye be of those who are endowed with insight. Those who read the Bayan yet deny the verses of the All-Merciful—these are they against whom the word of punishment hath been fulfilled, and they shall soon enter the fire. Be ye My trusted ones among My creation, My chosen ones among My creatures, and the dawning-places of My light among the worlds. Thus have We imparted unto you the word of truth and revealed unto you that whereby your hearts and souls may find tranquility, and ye may be of those who are steadfast.

The copy of the revelation that was written before the Face hath been sent. Copies of God's Tablets should be sent to all cities, and copies of all should be preserved in your presence. Blessed art thou for having attained unto the lights of the countenance of thy Lord. Upon thee be the glory of God and His splendor, then His remembrance and the remembrance of all the worlds.

## BH03710: Prologue to the Lawh-i-Mubahilih {.unnumbered}

It will have been known to the friends of God that one day the antichrist arose with a new scheme, in order to sow doubts in the hearts of the servants. In Edirne he advertised his intention to the Persians, saying,

> "Today we have resolved that he shall come to the Sultan Selim mosque, and we also shall attend, and shall make the truth manifest. Thus might truth be distinguished from falsehood."

Mir Muhammad Shirazi became informed of this pronouncement, and in turn apprised Aqa Mirza Muhammad Quli. The latter repeated it in the most glorious Presence. When He was informed, He departed that very hour and set out for the above-mentioned mosque. There are more details, but we shall mention only those necessary to telling the story. He said to Mir Muhammad, "Go and inform that person that I am waiting in the mosque." The aforementioned Mir Muhammad gave the news to that accursed one. Azal excused himself, saying that it was not possible that day: "The appointment will have to be fixed on another day."

Then Mir Muhammad said to that wicked one,

> "You yourself chose these arrangements. You stated a preference for this matter. You wrote a document saying that whoever did not appear today is false and far from the truth. Then how can any word of yours be depended upon?"

In short, He stayed at the mosque until sundown, but that wicked one avoided coming. As He passed through the market, the tongue of God addressed Mir Muhammad with these holy and eternal verses. All the people heard it, and were astonished at their revelation. This is the content of the aforementioned discourse:

When we heard, We proceeded from Our house with manifest sovereignty. We said,

> "O Muhammad, the spirit hath departed from its seat and along with it the spirits of the pure ones went forth, as did the realities of the Messengers. In truth, thou shalt behold the people of the most transcendent scene above My head. Then in My grasp are the proofs of the prophets. Then open your eyes. This is ʿAli [the Bab], then Muhammad, the messenger of God, who hath risen above the horizon of the House with evident sovereignty and come unto you with all the verses from God, the mighty, the Omnipotent."

Say: Were all the clergy and mystics on earth, and all the kings and emperors, to be gathered, I would stand before them and recite the verses of God, the king, the glorious, the wise. I am he who fears no one, even should all who are in the heavens and the earth assemble against Me. The very verses have humbled themselves before my countenance, and all sounds are submissive before my most wondrous and enchanting melodies. This is My hand, which God hath rendered white for all the worlds. And this is My staff. Were We to cast it down, it would swallow up the entire creation. All that hath been created between the heavens and the earth is but a handful of clay to thy Lord.

Go, Muhammad, to the concourse of idolaters and say, "The youth has come to you, accompanied by the hosts of revelation and inspiration. The kingdom of the Cause marches before Him, and behind Him are the tribes of the Concourse on high and the inhabitants of the cities of eternity, then the angels who are near." Say: Fear God, and do not oppose the one by whose command every wise decree was ordained. Then come into the presence of God with your ropes and your staffs and with whatever you possess, if you are able to do so. We go now to the house of God that was erected by one of the kings and named "Selim." I, alone, have come to you from the dawning place of eternity with a great, a most great announcement. I shall wait until the sun sets in the west, so that perhaps my opponents will find the opportunity within themselves to repent.

Know that God forbade his friends from meeting with the idolaters and hypocrites. Nevertheless, We departed from Our house depending upon God, gaze set toward the precincts of the Cause, so that thereby the heedless servants of God might be made aware. Those who have denied God or joined partners with him shall never believe in God, even should he bring them the sacred scrolls, or the hosts of the Invisible, or the proofs of the Messengers, and meeting with God only increases them in their oppression and unbelief....

He whom the idolaters have taken to themselves as their lord, whereby they have risen in opposition to God, the mighty, the august, the beautiful—he was just like any of the servants. He used to come into My presence morning and night. Then there wafted upon him from the region of his base self the gales of passion, as a result of his past behavior. Finally, they cast him down from his seat and abandoned him in the lowest depths. We had made his name renowned among the servants for a secret reason of our own. In truth, your lord is ruler over what he desires.

Also, there is a man by the name of Hasan Aqa in that land, a tobacconist. The antichrist was with him when he issued the aforementioned challenge. The text was written out with his knowledge. Indeed, in reality on that day the truth was fulfilled and perfect. Rather, it became most seasoned and most perfect.

When Mir Muhammad came into the presence of the Beauty of God, he said, "I informed that accursed one (that is, Mirza Yayha), that Baha'u'llah was waiting in the mosque, and I said, You should come and demonstrate your own truth.' That accursed one said, Today it will have to be postponed. Choose another day."'

Afterwards the tongue of God spoke forth, saying that with God it had been known that that scoundrel would not appear, and the purpose was to complete the proof. Rather, the proof had been complete from pre-eternity against those deniers of the beauty of the lord of the worlds.

The beauty of God departed from the mosque. It so happened that the store of the aforementioned Hasan Aqa was on Baha'u'llah's route. When he arrived at the store, the tongue of God said,

> "Based on the decision that the gentleman had announced in his proclamation, the countenance of the All-Merciful presented himself, whereas the idolaters failed to honor their own agreement."

The next day, this sublime pronouncement was issued to Hasan Aqa. But that accursed one gave it no attention. The text of the letter is as follows:

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

This is a letter from this youth to all who are upon the earth. Worship none but God, the king, the exalted, the mighty. Thus has the decree been revealed in all the tablets from the powerful, the Omnipotent.

We heard that some of our opponents desired to come into the presence of this youth. Say: Come, and do not delay! We have appointed as the meeting-place the house of God, which was erected by one of the emperors, and was called "Selim" in the kingdom of names, if you but knew. We have selected as the days for the meeting Sunday and Monday. God was a witness to what I say... He is the one intended by your lord, the knowing, the wise.

## BH00682: Suriy-i-Hifz {.unnumbered}

This hath been sent down for Muhammad, that he might praise his Lord and be numbered among them that render praise, mentioned in the Tablets of Glory. He is the Ever-Abiding, the Most Glorious.

This is a Book wherein is mentioned that which the Spirit hath inspired Me, and verily it is a revelation from God and a sign of His remembrance unto them who have acknowledged God and His verses. It guideth them unto the Path, and increaseth naught for the idolaters save manifest loss. This, verily, is the Path of God in the heavens and on earth, and His Hidden Book for them that are in the kingdom of Command and Creation, and His Treasured Scripture for them that are in the realm of the All-Glorious, and the Manifested Tablet for all who dwell on earth. Through it God's favor unto His creation is perfected, and His mercy encompasseth all worlds.

O peoples of the earth! Hearken unto that which God teacheth you in the Tablets, and follow not the ways of the most abject. Do that which ye have been commanded in the Book, then shun the ways of the corrupt ones who, when they found Us possessed of sovereignty and power, said "We believe in God and in what hath been sent down unto Thee," but when We entered prison they turned away and disbelieved, and were among the idolaters.

Say: God hath dominion over His creation and is supreme above His creatures, and nothing escapeth His knowledge. He watcheth over every soul. Say: Do ye deny the verses of God after which, were God to erase their traces and remove what ye have been given of the verses, ye would find no way for yourselves, nor any guidance? Fear God, O people, and deny not the proof whereby ye have known the path of God, the Sovereign, the Mighty, the Powerful.

Say: O people! When We found you heedless of God's Cause and envious in your hearts, We departed from your midst and changed Our garment, that ye might rest in your places and not commit that which would cause the Cause to lose its sanctity and honor among the servants. Thus were We among the doers. Yet ye showed no shame, but rather imputed to the Beauty of the All-Merciful that which Satan had whispered in your hearts, and were among the slanderers. From you and from your pens came that from which the denizens of the heavens and earth declared themselves clear. Ye attributed every evil unto Me, though God had made Me sanctified above all things and purified from aught else but Him, and sent Me from the Dayspring of Holiness with manifest sovereignty.

Say: Fear God! If ye believe not in Him and in the Manifestation of His Self, war not against Him, and be among the God-fearing. Attribute not what is within your souls unto the Self of God, and follow not the path of those who turned away from the Manifestations of the Cause and denied them until they slew them with grievous wrong.

O people of Baha! Keep yourselves apart from such as these, and turn not unto a people with whom God is wroth and whom He hath seized with vengeance from His presence. He, verily, is the most severe in punishment. Hasten unto God's good-pleasure and His satisfaction, then take up your abode in the secure station of this mighty Stronghold. Beware that ye draw not nigh unto them who have denied all the verses, whose eyes are veiled from My remembrance, and whose ears are wrapped in coverings from hearkening unto My holy, wondrous Words.

Say: When We found the earth of hearts barren of the vegetation of knowledge and wisdom, We then caused to descend from the clouds of grace that which made them stir and swell, bringing forth every noble kind. Rejoice, O people of the Bayan, in this Garden which hath appeared at the heart of Paradise, and deprive not yourselves of the wondrous knowledge ordained for you.

I am but a servant who hath believed in God and His verses, and I remind you of what God has inspired me through His grace, and guide you to the paths of those who are near. He who believes in Him and turns to God does so for his own sake, and he who turns away does so to his own detriment. My duty is but clear delivery of the Message.

O people! By God, besides Whom there is no god, I have indeed sacrificed my soul and spirit for the Cause of God, my Lord and the Lord of the worlds. We have raised the Cause to a station beyond the reach of the hands of harm and the hands of the idolaters. Thus has God established His Cause through His words and His sovereignty, and the deeds of the corrupt have been rendered vain.

When my brother witnessed that the sun of certitude had dawned from the horizon of utterance through this Youth, Who stood at the center of all creation with the adornment of the All-Merciful, he emerged from behind the veil of concealment and rose up to war against the Beauty of the All-Glorious, becoming one of the antagonists. He pronounced against me what his self and passion commanded him. Then the hosts of victory descended from the direction of a mighty throne, and the vanguards of divine protection appeared from the horizon of glory. God thereby protected me in truth and aided me through the power of might and authority, and His victory was near to those who do good.

When he found himself disappointed in what he desired and dejected in what he sought, he devised another stratagem, whereby all names were disturbed in their kingdoms, and all existence, both seen and unseen, wept at what befell my soul—and God was witness over him and me. When We found him in such a state, We departed from among them alone, relying upon God, the Powerful, the Almighty.

When he saw that the Cause had become renowned among these emigrants who had believed, he wrote tablets to various lands wherein he mentioned what he had perpetrated, seeking thereby to instill hatred for the Youth in people's hearts. Would that he had been content with this and been among those who rest! Thereafter he complained about the Youth to every soul to cause confusion about the Cause among the servants, thereby violating my honor and the honor of God, the Powerful, the Exalted, the Wise.

O people of the Bayan! Be fair within yourselves, speak with pure truthfulness, and be among the truthful ones. Most of you have associated with me and know my character—has anyone witnessed from me anything that would trouble their soul? No, by Him Who sent me with the truth, if you are among the fair-minded! I have been forgiving to the penitent, concealing toward the transgressor, merciful to the one who returns and repents, compassionate to the disappointed, and a refuge for the fearful—to this every fair-minded and discerning one bears witness.

Is there anyone among you who would deny this bounty? No, by my true Self, except one who denies all God's favors and follows the paths of the deluded! Would one who desires neither harm nor sorrow for anyone desire harm for his brother? Therefore, investigate and be among those who speak the truth and do not transgress the decree of truthfulness, even if the swords of the idolaters should fall upon him.

By God, the Truth! When my brother found that the hearts of the pure ones were filled with the love of God and the Manifestation of His Self, he desired to turn hearts away from the holy direction, after We had protected him for twenty years from the harm of every harmful one—and you were among the witnesses.

Say: O people of the Bayan! Deny not what you have witnessed with your own eyes, and follow not the paths of fancy. Rend asunder the veils of idle fancy through the power of might bestowed by Us, then enter the paradise of certitude and be among those who rejoice therein.

Thus have We informed you in brief concerning that which hath befallen Us, lest ye be heedless thereof and your feet slip from the path of God, the Mighty, the Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

And thou, O servant, arise to serve the Cause of God and fear no one. Convey unto the people that which God hath conveyed unto thee through His messengers. He will verily protect thee from the harm of all peoples. Strive thou to purify thyself from the defilements of the world and to adorn thyself with the attributes of God, the Mighty, the Dominant, the Powerful, the All-Seeing. Verily, if thou doest that which We have commanded thee, thou shalt become one who teacheth the people through deeds rather than words—and this is the most excellent teaching, if thou be of them that know.

Say: O people of the earth! Come with deeds done purely for God, the True One. The days of words have passed and the time for deeds hath come. Thus hath the matter been decreed by the Sovereign of all causes, if ye be of them that act.

Say: O people! Be as the signs of God amongst His servants and His traces in His lands, that through you the face of His Cause may be illumined amongst all creation. Thus have We informed thee and counselled thee that thou mayest take counsel within thyself and counsel the people with that which thou hast been commanded by the All-Knowing Judge. May the mercy that hath encompassed all created things rest upon thee, that thou mayest remain steadfast in the Cause of thy Ancient Lord—thou and those that are with thee among them whom God hath brought forth from behind the veils of fancy and guided unto the shore of mighty certitude. Praise be unto Him Who guideth all the worlds to the paradise of His wondrous Name.

## BH00366: He is God, exalted be His station in uniqueness… {.unnumbered}

### Section 1: “He is God, exalted be His station…” {.unnumbered}

He is God, exalted be His station in uniqueness above all contingent beings! By His mighty and irrevocable Word He distinguishes between all created things, and verily He is the One who has power over whatsoever He willeth, and He is the All-Glorious, the Most Glorious.

Thy letter hath come into the presence of the Throne, and toward it have turned the eyes of God, the Sovereign, the Almighty, the All-Powerful. The Countenance of God hath been directed towards it as a grace unto thy soul, a bounty unto thine essence, a mercy unto thy being, and a favor unto thy reality. This is that whereunto nothing can be compared amongst all that hath been created between the heavens and the earth.

We have heard that wherewith thou didst call upon thy Lord, the Almighty, the Most Exalted, the Mighty, the Inaccessible. We have learned that which the Spirit of the Command cast into thee, and whereby the Holy Spirit strengthened thee, and the Most Great Spirit spoke within thy illumined breast. Therein didst thou call upon God, thy Lord, with the sweetest of melodies, as though thou hadst heard the songs of the Dove upon the branches of the Tree of Glory, and recognized the melody of God from the Ultimate Tree and the Lote-Tree beyond which there is no passing. Well is it with thee for having drunk the wine of inner meanings from the hands of the immortal youths, and for being among those who have attained.

We shall therefore answer thee from the direction of the Throne with verses which render every possessor of knowledge powerless, and by a single letter whereof are created worlds the knowledge of which none comprehendeth save God, thy Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

Thou didst call upon God at the beginning of thy letter saying:

> "Glory be unto Thee, Who hast glorified Thyself beyond the glorification of all else but Thee, and none hath any way unto Thy call and Thy good-pleasure."

O thou who art the manifestation of Our Name, the Generous! Bear thou witness that He hath ever been and that there hath been naught else besides Him. He hath thus glorified His Self through the glorification of His Essence, and glorified His Essence through the glorification of His Self. He hath sanctified His knowledge beyond the knowledge of all contingent beings, and none hath any way unto Him. He hath ever been in the heights of grandeur and glory, and in the summit of loftiness and majesty. That which the mystics know and the perceivers perceive—this is but a creation created by His command and returneth unto the seat of that revelation wherewith We have revealed Ourselves unto all contingent beings. Whoso turneth towards it reflecteth the revelation of his Creator and ascendeth unto the station of nearness, and whoso depriveth himself thereof is indeed cast upon the earth of forgetfulness. Thus doth the Tongue of the All-Merciful speak at this moment, that thou mayest be of them that know.

Bear thou witness at this moment that His Self hath ever been sanctified beyond the knowledge of every knower, the learning of every learned one, the perception of every perceiver, and the attainment of every seeker, and shall ever remain as He hath been. Verily, He is the Peerless, the Most Exalted, the Inaccessible, the Mighty, the Most High. That which His servants attain unto—this is the station We have created for them through them, by themselves. Thus have We detailed in all the Tablets, and thus do We detail at this moment in truth, that it may be a remembrance from Us to them that remember.

We have accepted from thee this glorification and have sent its fragrances to the most exalted Paradise, wherefrom the people of the holy realm have inhaled them, that thou mayest be of them that receive glad-tidings. O joy be unto thee for that thy tongue hath been loosened and hath spoken that which the Spirit spoke, and hath testified before God with a testimony that hath caused the spirits of the Concourse on High and the realities of the sanctified ones to rejoice. Detach thyself from the world, then take comfort in the remembrance of thy Lord, that God may cause to flow from thy tongue rivers of Kawthar and Salsabil. By My beauty! A single drop thereof is better in the sight of thy Lord than all that is treasured in heaven and stored on earth.

Thus do We cast upon thee that which shall make thee independent of all the worlds. Therefore give thanks unto God, thy Lord, in that He hath heard thy call and accepted thy glorification and revealed unto thee in this Tablet that which is hidden from the eyes of the ungodly. Hearken unto that which is revealed, then take the Book of God with authority from Him, then recite it with the melodies of the Spirit. Let thy heart be drawn unto Him, and the hearts of those who glorify God in the depths of sanctity and who, at all times, are engaged in a wondrous remembrance.

And thou didst call upon thy Lord with another call, and it is this: I call upon Thee, though I am aware of this, with my inner and outer tongue, my manifest and hidden being, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee. From time immemorial Thou hast been sanctified above being called upon by any of Thy creation, and Thou wilt ever remain exalted above being invoked by any of Thy creatures. I have heard Thy call, and I bear witness to that which Thou hast testified through Thy Self, Thy Tongue, and Thy Pen, that He is God, there is no God but Me. I have created all things by My command, and brought all beings into existence through the influence of My Pen.

None besides Me can attain to the court of My glorious presence, and naught except Me can ascend to the heaven of holy knowledge of Me. For how can that which was created by My command attain unto My sanctified, purified, exalted, blessed, and luminous Self? Every call that ascendeth from all created things can rise no higher than the seat of revelation whereon We have manifested Ourselves through Our decisive, transcendent, mighty, and beauteous call. Beyond this, none hath any portion. Blessed is he who attaineth unto this exalted and glorious station.

We beseech God to enable thee to achieve that which thou hast uttered in thy letter, to make thee steadfast in His Cause, to aid thee with the power of His triumph amidst all peoples, and to grant thee the fruits of the Tree, each leaf of which speaketh that whereof not a letter hath been mentioned in all creation. Thus have We expounded the verses unto thee and given thee glad tidings of that which is treasured in the sanctified repositories of Him Who preserveth all things.

And thou didst call upon thy Lord again, and it is this: The believer is he who hath believed in Thy wondrous Manifestation, and the living one is he who hath been quickened by a breath of his recognition of Thy sovereignty, and the idolater is he who hath denied Thy radiant and resplendent Countenance, and the infidel is he who hath not been illumined by the dawning of the Sun of Thy manifest and glorious Visage. By My beauty! The Holy Spirit hath spoken through thy tongue, and God doth testify even as thou hast testified in thy letter, and calleth out from His ultimate dominion, nigh unto the divine Lote-Tree, the seat of His most exalted Throne: By God, the Truth! Whoso hath believed in Me hath attained all good, and hath drunk from the stream of certitude, and hath immersed himself in the oceans of knowledge, and his temple hath been adorned with the robe of grace from his Lord, the All-Merciful, and hath believed in all the Prophets and Messengers.

Say: When the temple of the All-Merciful was established upon the throne of His name, the All-Bountiful, the Spirit of Life was breathed into the realities of all creation and possibility. Whoso hath arisen to serve His Cause, acknowledged His sovereignty, and spoken His praise is alive with the life of God, thy Lord, and hath entered the eternal, everlasting, transcendent and mighty City of Oneness, the All-Glorious, the Most Bountiful. And whoso hath turned away from the Spirit of God and His breathings, the Spirit hath been taken from him and his name shall not be mentioned before the Throne, and he shall be of those who have no remembrance, no name, and no trace, and who abide within the veils of their own selves among the dead.

Say: O people! Fear God and associate not partners with Him in Whom ye have believed. Whoso associateth partners with Him hath associated partners with Manifestations who have no beginning and no end, and is recorded among the idolaters in the preserved tablets of holiness. Say: O people! Beware lest ye deprive yourselves of the grace of God and the wondrous tokens of His mercy.

### Section 2: “By the True God! Should anyone today engage…” {.unnumbered}

By the True God! Should anyone today engage in the worship of all who are in the heavens and on earth, and acknowledge in his heart the Manifestations of justice, and perform with his limbs every good deed, it shall profit him not so much as a grain of mustard seed unless he enters beneath the shadow of the Divine Countenance, becomes assured of God's grace and mercy, and arises to serve God and assist His Cause to the extent of his ability. This indeed is a revelation from Us, and We are the Revealer thereof. Say: Do ye make mention of God with your tongues while denying His sovereignty? Woe unto you, O heedless ones! If God accepted the faith of nations in the past, will He accept your faith? Nay, by My true Self! He will accept naught from anyone save after they have loved Me, and this is indeed a mercy unto all the worlds.

I called upon my Lord again and again, saying: I render thanks unto Thee for having created me when I was nothing, and for having fashioned me to seek what Thou lovest and art well-pleased with. Deprive me not, by Thy right, from the manifestations of Thy Most Great, Most Exalted Revelation. For Thou art the Doer of what Thou willest, and the Ordainer of what Thou desirest for what Thou desirest. Know thou that God hath accepted thy gratitude, and by thy thanksgiving do the dwellers of the pavilions of eternity give thanks. This is of His grace upon thee, and none hath preceded thee in this bounty. Be thou, therefore, in great thankfulness.

We created thee through the hands of might and power, as a mercy from Us unto thee and unto Our sincere servants. We fashioned thee with wondrous attributes, caused thee to speak in praise of My true Self, wafted upon thee the breaths of the Spirit, and made thee a remembrance from Us that thou mayest remind the people of that which thy Lord hath inspired thee. Be not thou of the patient ones. We delivered thee from the veils of fancy through Our sovereignty, preserved thee from the darts of idle fancies through Our power, bestowed upon thee that which established thee upon the throne of unity, saved thee from the hosts of Satan, and clothed thee in the garment of acceptance between the heavens and earth that thou mayest remember thy Lord within thyself and find rest in thy station. Strive then within thyself to be among the steadfast ones. By the True God! This is a matter at which all things are thunderstruck, every soul's lament is raised, and the mountains of the heedless are crushed.

We heard thy later call whereby were gladdened the hearts of those who sought the most exalted stations, who heard thy call and arose in thy love. Thus did We cause to flow from thy tongue that which is better than what is witnessed and seen, that thou mayest be among those firmly established. And it is this: By Thy glory, O my Lord and Master! Since Thou hast, through Thy mercy, enabled me without any merit to attain that for which none can adequately render thanks, enable me through Thy loving-kindness to be a prostrate servant before Thy Manifestation and a conquering soldier for Thy sovereignty. Through Thy power, make me such that whenever I encounter Thine enemies, I may vanquish them through a power from Thee and debate with them through an authority from Thy presence.

We have heard thy sweetest call and enabled thee through Our mercy and made thee worthy of the wondrous tokens of Our grace. We have therefore arrayed thee in the garment of names between earth and heaven and raised thee to the station of remembrance in the kingdom of creation. Arise then by thyself and fear no one, for thy Lord shall cause thee to triumph over whomsoever He willeth through His power and dominion from His presence. He is indeed the Strong, the Triumphant, the Almighty. Should all who are in the heavens and earth dispute with thee concerning the Cause of thy Lord, thou shalt not weaken. Draw strength from My Name, the Ruler, the Powerful, the Most Great, the All-Encompassing, for in His hand lies the kingdom of all things. He doeth what He willeth through His sovereignty, and ordaineth what He willeth through His command, and He, verily, is the Most High, the Almighty, the All-Wise.

Be not grieved by anyone's turning away, but remain steadfast in the Cause in such wise that the rejection of every infidel shall not harm thee, nor shall the cry of any crier prevent thee, nor shall the words that issue from the mouths of the idolaters sadden thee. By God, the Truth! Their association with God shall suffice them. Soon shall the fire of divine wrath be kindled in their hearts and shall return them to their abode in the nethermost depths, wherein they shall wail with the wailing of the distressed. And whenever they cry for help, they shall receive no succor. Thus hath the matter been ordained, and the sun of utterance hath shone forth from the horizon of revelation as a remembrance from One Who is mighty and beautiful.

Upon thee rest only My remembrance and the proclamation of My Cause. Whoso accepteth it doeth so for his own sake, and whoso turneth away—turn thou away from him and abide within a mighty stronghold. God shall soon distinguish between truth and falsehood, light and darkness, the fortunate and the wretched. Verily, He distinguisheth all things through a word from His presence, and He, verily, is the Powerful, the Ruler, the Resurrector, the Mighty, the All-Informed.

We have now made mention of some of what was inscribed in thy letter, and have deposited some of it in the treasuries of God's will. God shall fulfill it in truth and shall manifest it as He pleaseth. Verily, He is the Most Merciful, the Compassionate.

As to what thou hast mentioned concerning thy brother, We have previously sent tablets unto him that he might become mindful within himself and return unto God, thy Lord, and be of them that return. All this is of Our grace towards him. Should he accept, God will reward him for his deeds, and should he turn away, no blame shall rest upon thee. Grieve not over this, but be patient in all matters and be of them that are patient. Deal with him in such matters that the fire of sedition may not be kindled between you, for this is nearer unto grace, and We have ever been gracious. Moreover, counsel him with wisdom and goodly exhortation, and contend not with him lest enmity arise between you, until God shall bring about His purpose. This is My bidding unto thee; act according to what thou hast been commanded by One Who is mighty and ancient. Perchance thereby love shall be generated in his heart, though thy Lord well knoweth what is hidden in the breasts, and whatsoever He commandeth His servants is but a grace from His presence. Verily, He is independent of all worlds.

Spirit, light, glory and splendor be upon thee and upon them that walk with thee on a straight and glorious path.

Then make mention unto thy merciful brother: Say: O servant, remain steadfast in the hour when every light is darkened, every sun setteth, every soul is perturbed, everything waileth, every pillar is demolished, the pillars of every believer are shaken, and the faces of all mankind are transformed save those whom thy Lord willeth, for He, verily, is the Most Merciful, the Compassionate.

O Rahim! We have sent thee a tablet aforetime, then after it another tablet, as a grace from Our presence and a mercy from Us unto thee, that thou mayest be of the thankful. Look upon what hath been revealed unto thee with the eye of thy heart. By God! The sign of God shineth in all things besides Him even as the Sun of eternity shineth from the Most Exalted Horizon, yet the people are heedless within themselves and are of them that are negligent. Cast away what is in the hands of men, then take what is with thy Lord, then be content therewith apart from all the worlds. Thus have We commanded thee in truth and cast upon thee through grace, and verily the grace of thy Lord hath ever been truly magnificent.

## BH01361: Gul va Bulbul (The nightingale and the owl) {.unnumbered}

In the Name of the Friend! To God belongs the Most Exalted Similitude!

The spiritual rose hath appeared in the divine Ridvan at the advent of the spring of inner meanings, yet the outward nightingales remain deprived. The rose proclaimeth: "O nightingales! I am your Beloved, and I have appeared in the fullness of My hue and fragrant breath, and in My transcendent grace and freshness. Consort ye with the Friend and flee not from the Beloved." The metaphorical nightingales respond: "We are from the people of Yathrib and are accustomed to the rose of Hijaz, while thou art of the people of Truth and hast unveiled thyself in the garden of ʿIraq."

The rose replied: "It is now evident that ye have ever been deprived of the beauty of the All-Merciful and have never truly known Me. Rather, ye have known but walls and pillars and abodes. For had ye known Me, ye would not now flee from your Beloved. O nightingales! I am neither of Yathrib, nor of Batha, nor of Iraq, nor of Syria. Rather, I journey and wander through diverse lands—sometimes in Egypt, sometimes in Bethlehem and Galilee, sometimes in Hijaz, sometimes in Iraq and Persia, and now I have unveiled Myself in Adrianople. Ye are known for your love of Me, yet ye remain heedless of Me. It hath become clear that ye are ravens who have learned the ways of the nightingale. Ye wander in the realm of fancy and imitation, deprived of the blessed garden of unity.

Your example is like that owl who once said to a nightingale that the raven sang better than he. The nightingale replied: "O owl! Why hast thou abandoned justice and turned thine eyes from truth? Every claim requireth proof and every statement evidence. Here am I present, and here is the raven—let him sing that I may sing." The owl said: "This statement is unacceptable and rejected, for once I heard a sweet melody from a garden, and when I inquired about its singer, I was told it was a raven. Moreover, I saw a raven fly from that garden, so I was convinced the speaker spoke truth."

The hapless nightingale said: "O owls! That was not the raven's song but mine, and now I shall sing for thee that very same melody, nay better and more wondrous still." The owl replied: "I pay no heed to such words, nor do I accept such statements, for thus have I heard from my forebears and peers. Moreover, that raven is present and holds documentary evidence. If it were thee, how is it his name became renowned?" The nightingale said: "O unjust one! The hunter of malice lay in ambush for me, and the sword of tyranny pursued me from behind. Thus was the raven's name spread abroad while I, through the very intensity of my manifestation, remained hidden, and through the very perfection of my song became known as silent. Yet those possessed of hearing can distinguish the melody of the All-Merciful from the croaking of ravens. Now observe thou the essential voice and tune, that the truth may become manifest unto thee."

O ye who appear as nightingales! Ye seem like that owl who would not exchange a particle of fancy for a hundred thousand certainties, nor trade a single word of hearsay for the realm of direct vision and revelation. Hearken ye to the counsel of the Friend and gaze not upon the countenance of the Beloved through the eyes of strangers. Know Me through Myself, not through My dwelling place or abode.

While they were thus discoursing, suddenly from the blessed garden there appeared a new nightingale who entered in the divine garment and heavenly melody, and circling around the flower, said: "O nightingales! Though ye are nightingales in form, yet for some time ye have consorted with ravens and their ways have become manifest and evident in you. This Paradise is not your abode; fly away and depart! This spiritual flower is the trysting-place of nightingales who nest in the all-merciful realm.

Therefore, O human nightingales, strive to know the Friend and cut off the autumn's transgressing hand from this flower of the All-Merciful's Paradise. That is, O friends of God, gird up firmly the loins of service and protect the people of the world from the deceit and hypocrisy of the people of discord. And if ye appear among the servants with humility, submissiveness, and other qualities of truth, the hem of sanctity will remain pure and unstained from the calumnies of Satan and his manifestations, and the lies of the slanderers will become manifest and evident to all the peoples of the world. But if, God forbid, unseemly deeds be witnessed from you, all will revert to the holy court, and those very deeds will confirm the calumnies of the ungodly. And this is the certain truth, and praise be to God, the Beloved of the worlds."

## BH00814: This is an epistle from this servant, who… {.unnumbered}

In the Name of God, the Most Mighty, the Most Exalted, the Most Wondrous, the All-Glorious

This is an epistle from this servant, who is in attendance before the Divine Throne, unto them that have believed in God and whom God hath preserved from the tempests of temptation and the storms of trial, whose hearts He hath made steadfast and whom He hath sanctified from the doubts of such as have denied God and numbered among the idolaters...

Be it known unto the loved ones of God that this servant was, at a certain time, reposing beneath the shade of the mercy of my Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower, when there arrived a sealed letter. When I broke its seal, I observed that one of those who had turned away from God—he who was named Muhammad Ja'far and whom God had made an example to His vigilant servants—had addressed a petition to the Most Holy, Most Exalted Court. I took it up and opened it, comprehending all its contents...

This very moment I was summoned before the Throne. Thereupon I was asked: "Wherewith wast thou occupied?" I answered: "I was writing a few words in reply to the denunciations of the Infernal One." Whereupon, the Tongue of God bid me to write:

Hast thou not heard that My proof is Mine own Being, and My testimony is My Self, and My evidence is My Revelation, and that which floweth from My pen is a path to My knowledge, unattainable to all save those who have severed themselves from all things and passed straight through the world and all that is therein, aloof as a cloud? My proof hath ever been the revelation of My power which pervadeth all that are in the heavens and all that are on the earth. My verses I have made a path unto My knowledge, as a bounty on Our part unto all the people of the earth. Since my former Manifestation hath ordained the proof of this most holy, this most sublime and glorious Revelation to be the divine verses, therefore have We sent down verses from the heaven of the Divine Will. This is our abiding testimony unto all that are in the heavens and all that are on the earth.

Ere this Dispensation, verses alone had been singled out as a testimony unto all people. Such hath been Our bidding in all the Books of old. In this Revelation, however, and as a token of Our grace unto men, all the mighty signs, the conclusive proofs, the wondrous verses, the great evidences and the divine tokens have been sent down. Hereafter, it is in God's hands to decide upon the testimony of the Manifestations to come.

Erelong will He set down His command in His Tablets. We, verily, rule over all things and all affairs are within the grasp of Our might. We do as we will, and We ordain whatsoever We please. God, glorified be His remembrance, hath willed that, in this Dispensation, many a sincere believer who hath wholly turned unto Him shall give utterance to verses. Therefore shall We ordain the proof of the next Manifestation to be of a different nature, lest that he who produceth the verses may swell with pride before God, the All-Powerful, the All-Compelling, the Almighty. Consider how he whose tongue was, by My leave, unloosed to utter forth that which the servants around Me have uttered, waxed proud before God, notwithstanding that God had created him, had reared and saved him from the harm of his peers, and protected him under the wings of His most wondrous and incomparable grace. Such is Our bidding this night, and We command as We please at Our own behest. Powerful are We to accomplish whatsoever We will, and all besides Me are My creation.

O My people! Turn not away disdainfully from Him before Whose countenance stood the Concourse on high and be not of those who persist in proud disdain. Herewith conclude the words of God, the Most Sublime, the Most Wondrous, the Peerless....

## BH01597: Lawh-i-Kimiya 1 {.unnumbered}

...As to what thou hast asked concerning the Stone, know thou that it lieth scattered in every place, and within it We have ordained treasures that none knoweth save him whom We have taught knowledge from Our presence. Verily thy Lord is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed. It is one in itself yet from it appear multiplicities. Blessed is he who recognizeth it and witnesseth therein the power of God, and whom nothing preventeth from this straight path. It is God's treasure among His servants, the repository of mysteries among His creation, and the dawning-place of power to every discerning one who seeth. We have ordained within it a water which We have named the Fugitive, and We have nourished its earth with this water until there ascended by the power of the water the gold that was hidden within it. Verily it is the Red Sulfur and the Crown of Crowns, the Soul concerning which the wise have discoursed and in yearning for which multitudes have perished. It appeareth as water yet is fire in its nature and air in its essence. We have ordained earth within it and watered it with its water, and We have caused to grow therefrom the flowers of wisdom. Verily it is a mighty mystery.

Know thou that through the Stone alone is this work accomplished—nothing external entereth into it and nothing internal leaveth it. God hath made it a sign of His power among the worlds. It is the origin whereof the wise have spoken, and the mercury is the water that drippeth from it. This water is the key to the matter, if thou be of them that understand. When thou obtainest the key, open therewith the doors of thy Lord's treasuries within this Stone, from which rivers gush forth from the presence of One All-Wise, All-Informed.

This key appeareth as water but in its essence is fire. When thou appliest it to the earth, there ascendeth by the power of the water the gold of the wise. It hath been called by every name—it is the Most Pure Blood, the Penetrating Air, the Flying Gold, and the Moist Soul. It is the Active Essence through whose operation the hearts of the mature are bewildered.

When thou knowest the Stone and takest according to thy need, purify it, then separate it through fire. Then will appear to thee the four elements and thou wilt find thyself in great wonderment. Take its water, which is the Male, and wed it to its sister which is called Sulfur. After days pass the water will solidify itself and the child will appear. When thou seest it, give thanks to God, thy Lord and the Lord of all the worlds. It is the Red Egg, wherein We have ordained spirit, soul and body. We have named this Egg the Stone.

By God, We have unveiled what was hidden from the eyes of the learned, the mystics and the wise, and thy Lord is witness to what I say.

When thou attainest unto it and God bestoweth it upon thee, this is the first stage of operation. Take it by God's might and power, then extract from it the spirit, soul and body. Then purify each of these, then blend them in a blind alembic until they all become one thing. Then will the work be complete for thee and thou wilt see the power of thy Lord and find thyself bewildered at this mighty craftsmanship. Then if but a dirham of it be cast upon a thousand thousand of balanced bodies it will transform them, by God's leave, the Creator of creation, and thou wilt find them pure refined gold from which dross departeth.

Thus have We expounded for thee a sufficient exposition whereby the poor and needy may be enriched. It behooveth him who knoweth it not to make it for himself and to be of the God-fearing. By God, with thy Lord is the knowledge of both former and latter times.

And whatsoever thou hast heard concerning him who disbelieved in God—verily he hath fabricated. Say: O thou that liest! Bring forth thy proof, and thou shalt find thyself in manifest loss. He writeth somewhat of what he hath heard from Us, yet hath not grasped the outward meaning of that which hath proceeded from Our Pen and Our tongue. And thou wouldst bear Me witness to this, wert thou to be of the just. He knoweth not his right hand from his left, much less that which is concealed within the tabernacle of thy Lord's protection—the Almighty, the Preserver, the All-Knowing.

We have sent down diverse Tablets concerning all that thou hast asked. If thou desirest, examine them, that thou mayest be assured that all knowledge is with thy Lord, and none hath access unto it save His omniscient Self....

As for what thou hast asked concerning deeds, know thou that God thy Lord is the Creator, and the servants are the doers. Thus hath the matter been decreed and the judgment come from the presence of the Mighty, the All-Knowing. He hath created His servants and acquainted them with the pathways of His guidance and the ways of His Cause, and He hath created in them the power whereby they might traverse the paths of truth. Whoso walketh in that which his Lord hath desired, he verily hath attained salvation and security, and whoso turneth away, he verily hath disbelieved in God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting....

## BH04610: Know ye, O concourse of earth and heaven… {.unnumbered}

...Know ye, O concourse of earth and heaven, that I am He Who hath made all deeds to hang upon My good-pleasure... Yet My creatures have been heedless of the wondrous tokens of My loving-kindness, and have been veiled from the dawning splendour of My Face, and have strayed afar from the living waters of My mercy, from the Kawthar of My bounties, and from the Tasnim of My gracious favours.

...O soul! How long wilt thou refuse to quench thy fire, and suffer not thy blaze, thy flame, and thy burning to be stilled? How long wilt thou wander in the wilderness of error, and run to and fro in the desolate expanse of vain hopes? The more thou art fed, the more thy hunger increaseth; and the more thou art given to drink, the more thy thirst is multiplied. The fire of thy rebellion is not quenched, and the cloak of thy waywardness is not worn away. Frustrated is he who calleth upon thee; driven forth is he who summoneth thee. Thy steed is desire; thy gift is but a little. Thy traits are lusts; thy dispositions are sins.

Breaker of covenants, backslider from every praiseworthy advance! How long wilt thou not be calmed, O soul that commandeth unto sin? For thy habitation is built upon death. Thou hast rent the garment of equity, and hast smitten down champions through oppression. Thy injustice is a scorching wind, and thy shade a black smoke. Thy light is fire; thy light is illusion and shame. Thou leadest thine obedient ones unto hell, and thou givest thy followers to drink of scalding water. Thy home is the dust, and thy aspiration the Pleiades. How long wilt thou not be content, nor be satisfied, O beguiling, bedecked soul, and O adorned carrion...
